subject: Animation
title: Squash and Stretch: The First Principle
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Squash and Stretch: The First Principle.

hook.text: Squash and stretch is the most important animation principle. Without it, objects look rigid and lifeless.

buildup.text: When a ball hits the ground, it squashes flat. When it bounces up, it stretches tall. This creates life.

discovery.text: Disney's animators discovered this by studying how real bodies deform during motion and impact.

twist.text: The volume must stay constant. If a ball gets wider, it must get shorter. Breaking this rule looks wrong.

climax.text: Squash and stretch applies to everything — faces, bodies, even dialogue. It is the heartbeat of animation.

punchline.text: The secret to animated life is knowing when to squash and when to stretch.

quiz.question: What rule must be maintained when applying squash and stretch?
options: The color must change with each deformation
The volume of the object must stay constant — wider means shorter, and vice versa
The object must return to its original shape immediately

details.summary: Squash and stretch is the most fundamental animation principle: objects compress on impact and elongate during fast movement. It gives characters a sense of weight, flexibility, and organic life that rigid shapes cannot achieve.
details.whyItMatters: Squash and stretch is what makes animation feel alive rather than like moving cardboard. It is the first technique animation students learn and remains the most universally applied principle across all styles.
takeaways: Objects squash on impact and stretch during rapid movement
It creates the illusion of weight and flexible organic material
It is the most fundamental principle taught in animation education

faq.question: Does squash and stretch apply to realistic animation?
faq.answer: Yes, but subtly. Even realistic animation uses minimal squash and stretch on muscles, facial expressions, and fabric. The principle operates at every level of exaggeration from photorealistic to cartoon extremes.

faq.question: What is the key rule for applying squash and stretch?
faq.answer: Volume must remain constant. When an object squashes wider, it gets shorter. When it stretches taller, it gets thinner. Maintaining consistent volume is what keeps deformed shapes looking physically believable.
